method intersection(interval1: (int, int), interval2: (int, int)) returns (result: string)
    requires interval1.0 <= interval1.1 // start of interval1 is less than or equal to end of interval1
    requires interval2.0 <= interval2.1 // start of interval2 is less than or equal to end of interval2
    ensures result == "YES" ==> (intersectionLength(interval1, interval2) is prime) // if result is "YES", the intersection length is a prime number
    ensures result == "NO" ==> (intersectionLength(interval1, interval2) < 2 || !(intersectionLength(interval1, interval2) is prime)) // if result is "NO", the intersection length is less than 2 or not prime
    ensures result == "NO" ==> (interval1.1 < interval2.0 || interval2.1 < interval1.0) || intersectionLength(interval1, interval2) < 2 // if result is "NO", intervals do not intersect or intersection length is less than 2

// Helper function to calculate the length of intersection
method intersectionLength(interval1: (int, int), interval2: (int, int)) returns (length: int)
    ensures length >= 0 // the length of the intersection is non-negative
    ensures (length == 0) ==> (interval1.1 < interval2.0 || interval2.1 < interval1.0) // if length is 0, intervals do not intersect
    ensures length == (max(interval1.0, interval2.0) - min(interval1.1, interval2.1)) ==> (length >= 0) // length is calculated correctly

// Function to check if a number is prime
method isPrime(n: int) returns (prime: bool)
    requires n >= 0
    ensures prime ==> (n > 1 && forall i: int :: 2 <= i <= sqrt(n) ==> n % i != 0) // n is prime if it's greater than 1 and not divisible by any number from 2 to sqrt(n)
    ensures !prime ==> (n <= 1 || exists i: int :: 2 <= i <= sqrt(n) && n % i == 0) // n is not prime if it's less than or equal to 1 or divisible by some number from 2 to sqrt(n)
```
